research_question: How do raw-history context, vector retrieval, and running summaries compare in answer accuracy, token usage, and latency on LongMemEval, and what failure modes does each approach produce?

raw_history.planned_behavior: Keep the most recent complete turns within a fixed input token budget; drop oldest complete turns first when it doesn't fit.
raw_history.hypothesis: Older evidence needed for early-session questions may be removed by truncation.

vector_retrieval.planned_behavior: Chunk history (per exchange or bounded turn group), embed chunks and the question, retrieve the top-k most similar chunks as memory.
vector_retrieval.hypothesis: Semantically relevant-looking chunks may omit a session needed for the answer, especially for updates or multi-session reasoning.

running_summary.planned_behavior: Process sessions chronologically; after each one, update a bounded summary without seeing the eventual test question.
running_summary.hypothesis: Compression may drop fine-grained details or retain facts that a later session invalidated.

per_approach_allowed_to_vary: actual formatted prompt length (record the difference)
comparison_rules.summary_and_index_construction: must not see the future test question
comparison_rules.reference_answers_and_evidence_annotatio: evaluation only, never fed into the memory pipeline

model_and_runtime.runtime_version: Ollama 0.34.0 (Homebrew), default settings: flash attention off, fp16 KV cache. (OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1 + OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0 were tried first on Homebrew's own suggestion and reverted after measurement - see runtime_settings_investigation below.)

context_and_history_policy.context_budget_rationale: Chosen for prompt-eval throughput, not just memory: flash-attention+q8_0 (Homebrew's suggested settings) allowed up to ~80K context 100%-GPU-resident but measured only ~37 tokens/sec prompt processing, making a single near-budget call take 20-30+ minutes - impractical across a pilot. Ollama's plain defaults (flash attention off, fp16 KV cache) measured ~107 tokens/sec (~3x faster) but fit less context before spilling off the GPU. 32,768 is comfortably 100% GPU-resident (9.1GB, ~6.9GB headroom) under the fast default settings, with a worst-case single prompt-eval around 5 minutes. Both paths are well under the paper's own ~115,000-token setting either way; decided with the user rather than unilaterally since it affects timing for the rest of the project.

runtime_settings_investigation.method: POST /api/generate with a trivial prompt at each num_ctx, then `ollama ps` for memory/CPU-GPU split; throughput measured from prompt_eval_count / prompt_eval_duration on an 8,194-token test prompt, cross-checked against llama-server's own logged 'tokens per second'

context_and_history_policy.history_retention_rule: drop oldest complete turn until formatted prompt + output_token_limit fits the context budget
context_and_history_policy.token_counting_method: Current shared runner uses a conservative UTF-8 byte upper bound plus 256 template tokens when fitting; runtime prompt_eval_count and eval_count are recorded separately. This underuses the context ceiling and replaces the archived baseline calibration probes. Old smoke results are not reused.

data_and_pilot_sample.pilot_selection_method: up to 2 examples per reporting group (question_type, with question_id ending in _abs split out as 'abstention'), random.Random(42), ~14 questions expected

measurement_and_grading.timing_boundary: wall time from memory selection/retrieval start through complete answer; memory-construction time recorded separately
measurement_and_grading.token_fields: use the runtime's own returned token counts; mark unavailable values as missing, never as zero
measurement_and_grading.grading_rubric_pilot: Pinned official LongMemEval category-specific evaluator; no automated accuracy until a consistently graded complete set is imported. Manual spot checks are qualitative only.
measurement_and_grading.grading_method_full_run: TBD - LongMemEval repo's model-based evaluator (JSONL with question_id + hypothesis) for the larger run; audit a manual sample
